lessons: Prioritize immediate, high-impact statements over descriptive context; lines like 'Fresh pineapple is literally eating you back' outperform slower setup sentences.
Eliminate repetitive script pacing; retention drops significantly when content is restated (e.g., Highway Guardrails and Tuna videos), suggesting viewers leave if they hear a point twice.
Ensure technical explanations are concise; long scientific explanations, even if interesting, cause sharp drops at the 20-30% mark in almost all videos.
Strategic use of countdowns/pauses may actually help, as seen in the high retention of '400 Degree Foil' and 'Car Windows', but only if the call to action is immediate.
Avoid filler transitions or 'Pause and guess' prompts unless the video has high pre-existing momentum; these often correlate with the second major drop-off point.
Leverage the 'Greenland Shark' model: establish extreme, counter-intuitive facts early to sustain retention deep into the video.
worst_moment_types: Redundant narration where a point is repeated within 10-15 seconds.
Slow-paced scientific setup that delays the 'why' (seen in the 0.10-0.15 drop-off in most samples).
Transition lines that ask the viewer to pause or wait, which disrupts the flow of a short-form video.
Technical jargon-heavy explanations delivered without immediate relatable context.
best_hook_types: Direct, aggressive claims (e.g., 'Fresh pineapple is literally eating you back').
Unexpected, high-stakes scenarios (e.g., 'This shark is older than the United States').
Immediate focus on physical sensations or personal interactions (e.g., 'biting into a fresh slice', 'smashed your elbow').
